overview: Origin Energy is one of Australia's largest integrated energy companies, retailing electricity, natural gas, LPG and internet to almost 4.9 million customer accounts while owning and operating an 8.6 GW power generation portfolio spanning coal, gas, and a fast-growing renewables/battery-storage fleet. Beyond domestic energy retailing and generation, Origin holds a 27.5% interest in Australia Pacific LNG (APLNG), a major east-coast gas producer and Gladstone LNG exporter, and a 22.7% economic interest in UK-based Octopus Energy and its Kraken Technologies software platform, which was separated into a standalone business during FY2026. The company is ASX-listed (listed since 2000), reports on a June fiscal year end, and is navigating Australia's energy transition while continuing to generate substantial cash from legacy thermal and gas assets.

business_model.summary: Origin earns most of its EBITDA from Energy Markets (retail electricity/gas/LPG/internet plus owned generation and an emerging battery fleet), supplemented by its equity share of Integrated Gas (APLNG upstream production and LNG trading, an oil/JCC-price-linked earnings stream) and its equity share of Octopus Energy/Kraken (UK retail plus a fast-growing global SaaS licensing business for energy retailers). Energy Markets is the largest and most stable earnings base; Integrated Gas is highly cash generative via franked APLNG distributions but volatile with oil/LNG prices; Octopus/Kraken is currently near breakeven-to-loss for Origin's share but provides call-option-like upside via Kraken's global technology licensing growth.

revenue_streams.name: Energy Markets (retail electricity, gas, LPG, internet, energy services, generation)
revenue_streams.note: FY26 Underlying EBITDA $1,701m, up $298m YoY, ~upper end of guidance; largest and most consistent earnings contributor

revenue_streams.name: Integrated Gas - Share of APLNG (27.5% JV, upstream gas production + LNG export)
revenue_streams.note: FY26 Underlying EBITDA $1,620m, down $582m YoY on lower oil-linked (JCC) prices, moderating APLNG production (668 PJ) and lower LNG trading gains; FY26 cash distributions $911m fully franked

revenue_streams.name: Share of Octopus Energy / Kraken Technologies (22.7% economic interest)
revenue_streams.note: FY26 combined Underlying EBITDA a loss of $8m (improved from -$88m FY25); Kraken licensing revenue growing >20%/yr though currently loss-making as it scales; separated into standalone businesses during FY26 with Origin retaining economic interest only

business_model.customer_type: Predominantly B2C mass-market residential and small business energy retail customers (~4.9m accounts in Australia), plus wholesale/industrial gas and electricity customers, and B2B licensing (Kraken platform sold to other energy retailers globally)
business_model.geographic_mix: Energy Markets and Integrated Gas/APLNG are Australia-only (east coast gas basins, Queensland LNG export, national electricity market); Octopus Energy/Kraken exposure is UK-centric with expanding non-UK retail and global Kraken licensing markets

main_competitors: Woodside Energy / Santos (APLNG and east-coast gas supply competitors)
Shell / other Kraken-platform rival technology vendors in UK retail
competitive_position.market_position: Origin is the largest retail electricity and gas provider in the Australian east coast market by customer accounts (edging out AGL as the largest of the 'big three'), and via APLNG is one of the largest suppliers of domestic gas to Australian households, businesses and industry, and a major LNG exporter. Retail market for electricity is effectively a near-duopoly/oligopoly with AGL, plus EnergyAustralia and Red Energy as sizeable challengers.

moat_factors.description: Owns generation (coal, gas, renewables, batteries), retail customer relationships, and upstream gas (via APLNG) — natural hedge against wholesale price volatility that pure retailers lack

Largest customer account base in the National Electricity Market gives cost-to-serve and billing/collections efficiencies, and cross-sell (electricity, gas, LPG, internet, solar, batteries, EV charging)

moat_factors.factor: APLNG asset quality and contracted LNG offtake
moat_factors.description: 27.5% interest in a world-class, long-life CSG-to-LNG project with contracted export volumes and growing domestic gas supply role, though production is now in natural decline

Octopus Energy's Kraken software is a genuinely differentiated global SaaS platform now licensed to other retailers, giving Origin an indirect stake in a scalable, asset-light, high-growth technology business outside its core utility, though influence has diminished post-separation to a minority economic interest

Generation licensing, gas transport/pipeline access, retail authorisation and capital intensity of large-scale generation/battery development limit new entrant competition, though smaller retailers can still compete on price via the wholesale market

weaknesses: Thermal generation (Eraring coal, still ~2.9GW) is an ageing, high-emissions asset facing rising cost of extensions and eventual retirement/replacement capex

APLNG earnings are directly exposed to oil-linked (JCC) LNG pricing and AUD/USD, introducing commodity-cycle volatility Origin does not fully control (minority JV partner, not operator of upstream in all areas)
Octopus/Kraken stake has been diluted to a minority 22.7% economic interest following separation, reducing strategic control even as the businesses scale
Retail electricity/gas margins are politically sensitive and subject to government price caps/regulatory intervention during cost-of-living pressure episodes
July 2026 cyber/data breach (~900,000 customer accounts affected) highlights operational/reputational risk in a business holding large volumes of sensitive customer data

growth_drivers: Large-scale battery storage build-out: targeting 4-5 GW of renewables and storage by 2030, with 1.7-1.8 GW of battery projects under development (Eraring battery stages, Supernode tolled battery) and 710MW+ already generating revenue, capturing wholesale price volatility/firming premiums
Yanco Delta Wind Farm (~1.5 GW, ~$4bn+), awarded the largest single-project allocation under the federal Capacity Investment Scheme (CIS); transmission access secured, FID targeted mid-FY2027

Kraken Technologies global SaaS licensing growth (>20% revenue growth guided for FY26) as more energy retailers worldwide adopt the platform, monetizing Origin's minority stake without incremental Origin capital
Octopus Energy UK Retail scaling (targeting £25-50 EBITDA per customer) plus expansion into non-UK retail markets and Energy Services
Virtual Power Plant (Origin Loop) growth — over 1.5 GW / ~400,000 connected services, monetizing distributed rooftop solar/batteries/EVs
Electrification tailwind: consumer and business electrification (EVs, heat pumps, e-mobility) increasing electricity demand and cross-sell opportunities
Cost-to-serve productivity program targeting $100-150 million of savings by FY2026 vs FY2024
Continued (though declining) APLNG cash distributions funding capital returns and reinvestment while production optimisation partially offsets natural field decline

business.description: AGL, EnergyAustralia, Red Energy and smaller retailers compete aggressively on price and bundled offers in a near-commoditized market
Mid-life field decline at APLNG (FY26 production 668 PJ, guided lower again in FY27 at 625-670 PJ) requires continued drilling/optimisation capex just to partially offset natural decline

July 2026 breach exposed personal data of ~900,000 current/former customers, including some full bank account and ID numbers; ongoing investigation, regulatory scrutiny (OAIC, ACSC) and reputational/legal exposure

business.risk: Ageing thermal generation reliability and cost
business.description: Eraring coal plant extended to April 2029; continued operation carries unplanned outage, cost-overrun and workforce-transition risk as the asset ages beyond its original design life

financial.risk: USD/AUD and oil-price exposure via APLNG
financial.description: APLNG distributions and Integrated Gas earnings are directly linked to JCC oil-indexed LNG prices and AUD/USD; FY26 guidance assumed US$72/bbl JCC and 0.65 AUD/USD — swings materially affect distributions and Underlying Profit

Adjusted Net Debt/Adjusted Underlying EBITDA at 2.0x (H1 FY26), within the 2.0-3.0x target range but capex on batteries, Yanco Delta and Kraken investment ($210m committed) could push leverage toward the top of the range
FY26 Origin capex guided at $900m-$1,100m plus APLNG capex/opex of $2.9-3.2bn (100%); Yanco Delta alone is a $4bn+ project requiring equity partners

regulatory.description: Australian government has used the Gas Market Code of Conduct (price cap benchmark ~$12/GJ) and Australian Domestic Gas Security Mechanism (ADGSM) to intervene in domestic gas supply/pricing; government has flagged retiring these in favour of a new export-permitting framework, creating both relief and transition uncertainty for APLNG/Origin's gas marketing
Default Market Offer/price cap regulation and potential further government intervention during affordability pressure episodes could compress retail margins

regulatory.risk: Climate/emissions regulation and Climate Transition Action Plan scrutiny
regulatory.description: Origin's second CTAP received 94.67% shareholder support at the FY26 AGM, but net-zero-by-2050 and 2030 targets require continued capital reallocation from thermal to renewables/storage; failure to execute risks both stranded-asset and reputational/activist risk
Potential regulatory penalties or mandated remediation costs stemming from the July 2026 data breach under Australian privacy law

macro.risk: Wholesale electricity and gas price volatility
macro.description: Origin is directly exposed to swings in NEM wholesale electricity prices and east coast gas prices; FY27 Energy Markets guidance explicitly assumes lower wholesale electricity prices versus FY26, illustrating margin sensitivity
APLNG earnings and distributions swing with global LNG/JCC oil benchmarks, which are influenced by global supply growth (US, Qatar) and geopolitical factors

macro.risk: Renewables build-out cost inflation and delay
macro.description: Management explicitly noted the large-scale renewables/transmission build-out is 'proving more difficult, with projects taking longer, costs rising' — Yanco Delta economics described by management as 'very challenging' even with CIS support
Capital-intensive generation/battery investment program is sensitive to funding costs; moderate given AUD/USD hedges on APLNG-related debt

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian electricity demand is inflecting upward after years of flat/declining demand, driven by electrification (EVs, heat pumps) and data centre/AI-driven load growth, while the National Electricity Market undergoes a structural shift from coal to renewables/storage/gas-peaking firming capacity, supported by federal Capacity Investment Scheme underwriting.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. Retail energy demand is relatively defensive/non-discretionary, but earnings are cyclical/volatile through wholesale electricity price swings, APLNG's oil-linked LNG pricing, and generation asset availability (e.g., Eraring outages).
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — large capex program (batteries, Yanco Delta, sustaining capex) is debt-funded in part; APLNG-related USD debt is largely hedged back to AUD.
key_input_costs: Wholesale electricity and gas purchase costs
Network/transmission charges passed through to retail tariffs

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results: statutory profit $1,574m (+6% YoY), Underlying Profit $1,159m (-22% YoY) on lower Integrated Gas earnings, Adjusted Free Cash Flow $2,074m (+72% YoY); full-year fully franked dividend maintained at 60 cps; shares rose ~5-6% on the print as strong cash generation offset the earnings miss (Underlying EPS $0.352 vs consensus ~$0.361)

Cybersecurity incident disclosed: unauthorized access affecting ~900,000 current/former customer accounts (names, addresses, DOB, partial payment details); ~60 customers had full bank account numbers and ~100 had ID document numbers exposed; company notified ACSC, AFP and OAIC and is offering credit/identity monitoring

Announced extension of Eraring coal-fired power station operations to 30 April 2029 (from 2027) to support NSW grid reliability through the transition; management states this does not affect 2030 emissions targets or net-zero-by-2050 ambition

Signed agreement with Octopus Energy to waive exclusivity to the Kraken platform in Australia in exchange for an additional 1.5% equity interest in Kraken (~$190m pre-tax gain recognised), taking Origin's combined Octopus/Kraken economic interest to 22.7%

Octopus Energy and Kraken Technologies completed separation into standalone businesses; Origin committed ~$210m across a suite of transactions to lay the foundation for the separation while retaining a 22.7% economic (non-controlling) interest

H1 FY2026 results: revenue down 9% to $7,993m, statutory profit down 45% to $557m, Underlying Profit down 36% to $593m on lower Integrated Gas/APLNG trading gains and volumes/prices, plus a $65m reduction in Octopus Energy EBITDA; interim dividend held at 30 cps fully franked; Adjusted Net Debt/EBITDA 2.0x

Progressed the ~1.5 GW Yanco Delta Wind Farm (largest single-project award under the federal Capacity Investment Scheme), securing full transmission access; targeting FID by mid-FY2027; management describes project economics as 'very challenging' even with CIS support
Commissioned Eraring battery stages 1 and 3 (460MW/1,770MWh) and approved a fourth stage extension; Virtual Power Plant (Origin Loop) grew to ~1.6 GW across ~409,000 connected services
Board renewal continued with appointment of Fiona Hick and Stephen Mikkelsen as independent Non-executive Directors during FY2026

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Frank Calabria characterized FY26 as a 'solid full-year result,' with Energy Markets strength partially offsetting an expected decline in Integrated Gas earnings. Management flagged that Australia's energy transition is 'advancing, but not evenly,' citing rising costs, longer project timelines, and a challenging regulatory/community backdrop for large-scale renewables and transmission build-out (explicitly citing Yanco Delta's 'very challenging' economics even with Capacity Investment Scheme support). Guidance is explicitly conditioned on no material adverse change in market conditions or the regulatory/political environment.

bull_case: Vertically integrated model (generation + retail + upstream gas via APLNG) provides a natural hedge against wholesale price volatility that pure-play retailers lack, and FY26 Adjusted Free Cash Flow surged 72% even as headline earnings declined

Large-scale battery and renewables build-out (Eraring batteries, Supernode, Yanco Delta) positions Origin to capture rising firming/price-premium revenue as coal exits the NEM, with the largest single-project Capacity Investment Scheme allocation de-risking Yanco Delta's returns

Octopus Energy/Kraken stake (22.7% economic interest) offers optionality on a fast-scaling, high-growth global SaaS energy-retail platform (Kraken revenue growing >20%/yr) largely decoupled from Australian regulatory/commodity risk
Consistent, fully franked capital returns (60 cps FY26 dividend, ~5.7% yield) backed by strong operating cash flow and a balance sheet within its 2.0-3.0x leverage target
Structural east-coast electricity demand inflection (electrification, data centres/AI load growth) supports long-term volume and pricing tailwinds for Origin's retail and generation businesses
bear_case: Integrated Gas/APLNG earnings are volatile and now declining structurally as JCC oil-linked prices normalize and mature fields decline (FY26 production down, FY27 guided lower again at 625-670 PJ), reducing a historically large distribution/profit contributor

Energy transition execution risk is explicitly flagged by management as 'not linear' and 'increasingly challenging' — rising renewable/transmission build costs, permitting delays, and community pushback threaten the economics of flagship growth projects like Yanco Delta

Regulatory and political intervention risk remains elevated: east-coast gas market code/ADGSM reform, retail price caps, and cost-of-living-driven scrutiny could compress margins in both gas and retail electricity

July 2026 cybersecurity breach affecting ~900,000 customers creates reputational, regulatory and potential financial liability overhang, and highlights operational risk in a data-intensive retail business

Octopus Energy/Kraken stake has been diluted to a minority, non-controlling 22.7% economic interest post-separation, limiting Origin's strategic influence and dividend upside even as the businesses (and Kraken royalties) scale globally
Ageing Eraring coal plant, now extended to April 2029, carries ongoing reliability, unplanned-outage and cost risk as a legacy asset operated well beyond original retirement plans
